info.title: timezone.io API
info.summary: IANA time zones, named abbreviations, countries and cities, with live offsets, DST state and conversions.
info.description:
Every request needs a free personal access token from a verified timezone.io account, sent as a bearer token. The Free plan allows 100,000 requests a month at 5 a second; paid plans raise both (https://www.timezone.io/docs/rate-limits). Guides and worked examples: https://www.timezone.io/docs.

GET /lookup answers from time zone boundary data. Contains information from timezone-boundary-builder (https://github.com/evansiroky/timezone-boundary-builder), made available under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0 (https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). Boundary data © OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

get.description: A paginated, filterable list of IANA time zones. Rows are concise unless `detail=full`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Literal search across the IANA identifier and display name.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key. Prefix with `-` for descending.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Filter by standard UTC offset, within ±14:00: `-04:00` or bare minutes like `-240`.

parameters.name: abbreviation
parameters.description: Filter by abbreviation code such as `EST`, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: is_mainland
parameters.description: Keep only mainland (`true`) or outlying (`false`) zones.

get.description: One IANA zone in full detail: live time, standard offset and the next DST transition. The slash in the identifier is part of the path; encode `+` as `%2B`.

parameters.name: iana
parameters.description: IANA identifier, for example `America/New_York`.

get.description: A paginated list of named time standards (EST, CET, JST). Rows are concise unless `detail=full`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Literal search across code, name and slug.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Filter by the standard's UTC offset: `+01:00` or bare minutes like `60`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key. Prefix with `-` for descending.

get.description: One named time standard, by slug (always unique) or code. A code shared by several standards (AST, CST) returns `300` with candidates; narrow it with `offset` or `continent`, or re-request by slug.

parameters.name: abbreviation
parameters.description: Slug (`eastern-standard-time`) or code (`EST`).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated related data to embed: `timezones`, `countries`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Disambiguate a shared code by offset: `+03:00` or `180`.

get.description: A paginated list of countries and territories. Rows are concise unless `detail=full`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Literal search across name, `iso2`, `iso3` and slug.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: One ISO region (`Americas`, `Europe`, `Asia`, `Africa`, `Oceania`), case-insensitive.

parameters.name: sub_region
parameters.description: One ISO sub-region, such as `Western Europe`, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key. Prefix with `-` for descending.

get.description: One country by slug (`australia`) or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (`AU`).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Slug or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated related data to embed: `timezones`, `abbreviations`, `cities`.

get.description: A paginated list of cities with their live UTC offset. Rows are concise unless `detail=full`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Literal search across name and slug.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA identifier, for example `America/New_York`.

parameters.name: is_capital
parameters.description: Keep only capitals (`true`) or non-capitals (`false`).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `name`, or `offset` (the zone's standard UTC offset). Prefix with `-` for descending.

get.description: One city with its live local time and live sunrise, sunset and daylight length. Cities that share a name are addressed as `<slug>-<iso2>` (`barcelona-ve`).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: City slug.

get.summary: Convert a moment between time zones
get.description: Convert one moment from a source to up to ten targets. Every datetime carries its UTC offset and is pinned to the single `utc` instant; daylight-saving folds and gaps are disclosed in `ambiguity`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: One location token: IANA identifier, shorthand (`pt`), UTC offset (`UTC+2`), abbreviation slug or code, city, or country.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: 1–10 comma-separated location tokens, in the same formats as `from`.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: The moment to convert. A naked datetime (`2026-11-01T01:30:00`) is wall-clock time in `from`; an anchored datetime or Unix timestamp is an absolute instant. Defaults to now.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: How an ambiguous or skipped wall time is handled.

get.summary: Find the time zone at a point
get.description: The time zone at a latitude and longitude, on land or at sea, with the same `timezone` block as `/timezones/{iana}`, computed at `at`. Where two zones' boundaries overlap (disputed areas, and a few narrow slivers along borders and coasts in the source data), the one with the smallest area comes first and the others are listed in `alternatives`, except in Xinjiang, Abkhazia and Kalapani, where the administering authority's zone comes first. A point exactly on a border belongs to the zone east of it, or north of it on an east-west border. At sea the zone is `Etc/GMT±N`, whose sign is inverted: `Etc/GMT+3` is UTC-03:00.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Rounded to 6 decimals. Exponents like `5e-7` are read; commas, and spaces inside the number, are rejected.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180. Required unless `lng` is given.

parameters.name: lng
parameters.description: Alias of `lon`. Send one or the other.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Reserved for a later version. Any non-empty value is rejected with 422.

bearerAuth.description: A personal access token from https://www.timezone.io/api-keys (the account's email must be verified).

at.name: at
at.description: Compute the time-dependent fields at this moment instead of now: an ISO 8601 datetime (a naked one is read as UTC) or a Unix timestamp in seconds within years 2000–2100.

detail.name: detail
detail.description: `concise` rows, or `full` to return the detail shape per row.

observesDst.name: observes_dst
observesDst.description: Keep only results that do (`true`) or don't (`false`) observe daylight saving time.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The maximum number of requests allowed in the window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimit-Policy.description: The limits that apply to this account, as IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers quota policies: "burst" (requests per second, w=1) and, when monthly quotas are enforced, "monthly" (requests per calendar month in UTC).

RateLimit.description: What remains of each policy (r) and the seconds until it resets (t). The monthly r counts down to the quota; requests within a paid plan's 10% buffer are served with r=0.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. On a 429 it is about a second for the per-second limit; for the monthly quota it is at most 3600: check back hourly, or read RateLimit's monthly t for the reset (00:00 UTC on the 1st).

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp when the window resets.

MultipleChoices.description: The identifier matches more than one time zone. Re-request with one of the candidates.

Unauthorized.description: The token is missing, malformed or revoked.

Forbidden.description: The account's email address isn't verified.

example.message: Verify your email to use the API. Resend it at https://www.timezone.io/verify-email

NotFound.description: No resource matches the identifier in the URL.

TooManyRequests.description: The per-second rate limit or the monthly quota was exceeded. Over the quota, the message names the plan, says how to get more, and gives the reset date: "Your Free plan's 100,000 requests for September 2026 are used up. Upgrade at https://www.timezone.io/billing for more, or wait until the quota resets on October 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC."

ServiceUnavailable.description: No boundary data is installed. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

self.description: Null for a zone at sea such as `Etc/GMT+3`, which has no `/timezones` entry.

Current.description: The zone's state at the requested moment (now by default).

name.description: Friendly name of the standard in effect.

savings_seconds.description: How far clocks move for DST; 0 when the zone doesn't observe it.

next_transition.description: The next clock change, or null when none is scheduled.

AbbreviationCurrent.description: The standard's defining offset; `is_dst` is true for a daylight-saving standard.

counterpart.description: The standard/daylight twin (EST ↔ EDT), or null.

default_timezone.description: The zone a country resolves to when one zone is needed, or null.

sun.description: Computed for the local date of `at`. Sunrise and sunset are null inside the polar circles (daylight 1440 for polar day, 0 for polar night) or without coordinates.

self.description: Null for a fixed-offset zone such as `Etc/GMT-2`.

ambiguity.description: `resolution` and `note` are present only when the wall time was ambiguous or skipped.

is_ambiguous.description: The wall time occurred twice (a DST fold).

is_skipped.description: The wall time never occurred (a DST gap).

tzdb_version.description: IANA tz database release the answer was computed with.

query.description: The point that was looked up, rounded to 6 decimals.

kind.description: `ocean` where no country's zone applies (`Etc/GMT±N`): international waters, and the unclaimed part of Antarctica. `land` includes territorial waters.

reason.description: `overlap`: another zone's boundary also contains the point. `antimeridian`: the zone across the 180° line, for `lon=180` or `lon=-180`.

version.description: The boundary release that answered. A point's zone only changes when this does.

attribution.description: The credit the boundary data's licence (ODbL 1.0) asks for, with its URIs as plain text.

links.description: Page links for rendering a paginator.

anyOf.description: A named standard sharing the requested code.
A time zone matching the requested token.
